limitations: Two ordinary games repeat; no new full replay, wider roster, declared powers, paid Rites or Resummon coverage.
cProfile heavily instruments both runtimes; function fractions are candidate-selection evidence, not measured achievable unprofiled savings.
Stage timers describe one separate game per case per runtime; their wall times are not the 20-game throughput means.
CPython timing increase has no identified cause. Both uploads use the same engine, input manifest, worker, executable and recorded runtime options; snapshots/digests follow the stop time in both.
Allocation/GC conditions, CPU frequency, thermal state and competing load were not measured; no cause is assigned to the CPython variation.
Memory, policy selection, worker scaling and steady-state campaign throughput remain unmeasured.
decision: A bounded movement/registry-restoration experiment has identifiable work to remove, but this profile does not establish another quick 2–3x. Keep exact parity and matched within-runtime unprofiled timing as the decision gates; no engine change accompanies this record.
